topic: What beam management strategies are needed to mitigate efficiency fluctuations (>3 dB gain variance) across the 57-66 GHz band?
consensus_response: To mitigate efficiency fluctuations exceeding 3 dB in the 57-66 GHz band, adaptive beamforming techniques and optimization frameworks can be employed. These methods optimize system parameters like beamforming granularity to manage inter-beam interference and improve spectral efficiency. Digital beamforming provides more precise control over phase noise but requires advanced signal processing algorithms and increased computational complexity. Frequency domain equalization (FDE) techniques can also be used in conjunction with adaptive beamforming for efficient compensation of phase noise and inter-symbol interference (ISI). Furthermore, optimal antenna element spacing should balance the tradeoff between angular resolution and inter-element interference.
reference_context: The reference context provides various studies on mmWave frequencies, including the impact of path loss, phase noise, and mutual coupling on beamforming performance. The maximum beam gain in the 57-66 GHz band is reported to be up to 51.8 dBi, while the average satisfaction index for used bandwidth, carrier, and power are also discussed.
